question.problem:
In the figure below, $\overset{\longrightarrow}{AC}$ is the bisector of $\angle DAB$ and $m\angle DAB = 79^\circ.$ What is the measure of $\angle DAC?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191213/assets/8d02999cf6ae7ec69fee2cdac99b8dc214c59f1ed50bbf85bec6bec01f2212ef.png)
question.worked_solution:
An angle bisector divides the angle into two congruent angles with equal measures, so $m\angle BAC = m\angle DAC .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191213/assets/6e7c8ce2713441e633d7ecc3548c504d2522b4771eb6355217d6ab766a647b67.png)

Each of these congruent angles has a measure that is half the measure of the larger bisected angle. So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠DAC & =\frac{m∠DAB}{2} \\  & =\frac{{79}^{∘}}{2} \\  & ={39.5}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
